title: Mohammad Tasleem v. State of U.P. and others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Pritinker Diwaker, J.; Ashutosh Srivastava, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; pending clause 6.5 representation to be decided in three weeks, no merits.
headnote: The Allahabad High Court disposed of a writ against an electricity bill issued in the petitioner's father's name by directing the concerned officer to decide the pending clause 6.5 Supply Code representation within three weeks, if not already decided, strictly in accordance with law. Counsel for the licensee had no objection. The Court expressed no opinion on the billing dispute.
facts: Mohammad Tasleem filed a writ in the Allahabad High Court against a bill issued by the electricity board in his father's name. He claimed the family was paying bills regularly and that nothing was outstanding. He had already made a representation under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 to respondent no. 4, which had not been decided. He asked only that the officer be directed to dispose of that representation. Counsel for respondent no. 4 did not object.

holding_units.holding: A writ complaining of a disputed electricity bill may be disposed of, without any opinion on merits, by directing the designated officer to decide a pending clause 6.5 Supply Code representation within a fixed time and strictly in accordance with law.

principle_tags.application: The Court accepted the limited prayer and, with no objection from the licensee, directed respondent no. 4 to decide the pending clause 6.5 representation within three weeks if not already decided, strictly in accordance with law and without examining the billing dispute.

not_decided.point: whether the bill in the father's name was illegal or whether any dues were outstanding
not_decided.note: The Court expressly declined to express any opinion on the merits and left the representation to be decided strictly in accordance with law.
